verdict: The reader's note was accurate on nearly every printed value: I re-checked all 26 rows of Table 1 at 22 levels, all 16 rows of Table 2, Tables 3 and 4 and every text figure against the page images, and the values, units, levels and pages were right. Its main faults were small arithmetic slips in derived ratios and ranges, a few overstatements (C3 smallest on every body measure, T4/T5 narrowest canal of the column, TPL twice, sign conventions presented as stated), and unlabeled inference in the radiograph recipes. Its real omissions were definitional and came from Fig. 1, Panjabi's drawing: the cervical upper end-plate width is taken between the uncinate processes, and spinous process length runs from the upper end-plate centroid to the tip. It also lacked any check of which junction markers survive in the comparison series. Using the Panjabi values implied by Tables 1 and 2, the TPW steps at C7/T1 and T12/L1, the PL step at T12/L1 and the L5 pedicle rise are shared, while the T12/L1 pedicle-width drop and the L1 canal-area maximum are peculiar to this sample. The note now has all of these, every inference marked, ASCII only. The paper itself reports no anomalies and no numbering method, so it gives the sequence decoder nothing; its use is per-level means and SEs (n = 10) and population factors for a Chinese sample against Panjabi.

record.citation: S. H. Tan, E. C. Teo, H. C. Chua. Quantitative three-dimensional anatomy of cervical, thoracic and lumbar vertebrae of Chinese Singaporeans. Eur Spine J (2004) 13: 137-146 (issue not printed; Inference, from memory: issue 2). DOI 10.1007/s00586-003-0586-z. Copy read: greg's upload of 2026-10-28 19:54 UTC (Springer's PDF, file s00586-003-0586-z.pdf); sha256 begins 5e2b122b7e235174.
record.population: Singapore; 10 Chinese cadavers of Singaporean origin, dry bone; 220 vertebrae (C3 to L5, 22 levels per cadaver; Inference: n = 10 per level); mean age 65.7 years (56 to 77), mean weight 61.6 kg (50 to 70), mean height 1.66 m (1.59 to 1.72); sex not reported; no inclusion or exclusion criteria beyond origin. Compared with published white (Caucasian) series: Panjabi et al. 1991-1992 (all parameters of Table 2, PDIs), Zindrick et al. 1987 (PL, PDIs), McLain et al. 2002 (PL T1 to T6; 11 women and 7 men aged 62 to 85). p. 137 (PDF 1), p. 145 (PDF 9).
record.modality: Dry-bone cadaveric morphometry with a direct-contact 3D digitiser (stated accuracy 0.01 mm; make not named); specimen fixed by a screw in a 5 mm anterior hole, clamped, clay-stabilised; vertebral frame on the posterior body wall with origin at the upper end-plate centroid; linear and area measures on the plan view of best-fit planes, angles on the side view; each point the mean of ten hits, each parameter the mean of three readings. pp. 137-139 (PDF 1-3).
record.levels_covered: C3 to L5 (22 levels); pedicle length T1 to L5 only; no C1, C2 or sacrum, so no C2/C3 or L5/S1 junction data.

anomalies.variant: none reported (no transitional vertebra, rib count, LSTV, L6, T13, cervical rib or block vertebra mentioned)
anomalies.finding: No anomaly prevalence. 220 vertebrae = 10 cadavers x 22 levels, so no specimen contributed a missing or extra segment to the sample (Inference); whether such spines were screened out, and how levels were numbered, is not stated.

measures.name: End-plate width, upper and lower (EPWu, EPWl), mm
measures.definition: Transverse extent of the upper or lower end-plate along X in the front view. Fig. 1a (Panjabi's drawing) draws the cervical EPWu between the uncinate processes and EPWl across the whole lower body; lumbar EPWu spans the whole end-plate. Measured on the plan view of the end-plate best-fit plane.
measures.projection: dry bone, 3D digitiser, coronal (plan view of the end-plate plane)
measures.page: p. 138 (PDF 2) Fig. 1; p. 139 (PDF 3) Fig. 4; Table 1 pp. 140-141 (PDF 4-5)
measures.level_pattern: EPWu C3 13.8, C7 19.0, T1 24.7, falls to T4 22.5, rises to L4 42.0, dips at L5 41.6; EPWl C3 14.3, C5 15.9, C6 19.5, T1 27.1, minimum T5 23.8, L4 45.3, L5 43.7. Steps: C5/C6 EPWl +3.6, C6/C7 EPWu +3.2, C7/T1 +5.7 (upper) and +6.8 (lower). Lower wider than upper. Does not order T1 to T6 or separate L4 from L5.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi -10.2% (upper), -10.4% (lower); regional C/T/L about -14, -9, -10%; largest at C5 (-16.5% mean). Implied Panjabi C7/T1 EPWu step only 2.7 mm. pp. 142-144 (PDF 6-8).
measures.error: SE 0.0 to 0.5 mm; median CV about 3% (SD = 3.16 x SE, Inference); digitiser 1.28% at 20 mm.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: cranial or caudal end-plate surface of the body subregion, projected on its best-fit plane, extent along the frame X axis; at C3 to C7 stop the upper width at the uncinate bases.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph, end-plate line width (uncinate bases at C3 to C7); magnification applies; ratio to TPW or canal width is magnification-free.

measures.name: End-plate depth, upper and lower (EPDu, EPDl), mm
measures.definition: Antero-posterior extent of the end-plate along Z (Fig. 1 side views).
measures.projection: dry bone, 3D digitiser, sagittal or plan view
measures.level_pattern: Flat C3 to T1 (13.6 to 15.8); nearly linear rise T1 to T12 (EPDu 14.9 to 26.7); relatively constant lumbar (EPDu 27.5 to 30.8, EPDl falls 1.6 mm L4 to L5). Best measure to order T1 to T6.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi -15.6% (upper), -14.7% (lower); largest at T1 (-19.7% mean). pp. 142-144 (PDF 6-8).
measures.error: SE 0.1 to 0.6 mm; median CV 4 to 5% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: end-plate surface extent along Z at the frame midline (x = 0).
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, end-plate line length; magnification applies.

measures.name: Vertebral body height, anterior and posterior (VBHa, VBHp), mm
measures.definition: Distance between upper and lower end-plates at the anterior and posterior body margins along Y (Fig. 1 side views).
measures.level_pattern: VBHa 9.6 (C5) to 22.0 (L5); VBHp 11.2 (C3) to 23.1 (L2), then falls to 20.0 at L5. Posterior exceeds anterior in the cervical, thoracic and lumbar spine except L5 (L4 equal); VBHa/VBHp 0.85 to 0.95 C3 to L2, 0.97 L3, 1.00 L4, 1.10 L5. C7/T1 VBHp +2.2 mm.
measures.covariates: VBHp against Panjabi -4.0% (L -8.2%, L5 -12.7%); VBHa not compared. p. 144 (PDF 8).
measures.error: SE 0.1 to 0.7 mm; median CV 4.5% (VBHp) and 6% (VBHa), Inference.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: in the frame's mid-sagittal plane, Y distance between cranial and caudal body surfaces at the anterior and posterior cortex.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph; VBHa/VBHp is magnification-free.

measures.name: Spinal canal width (SCW), mm
measures.definition: Transverse width of the vertebral foramen in the top view; Fig. 1 draws it as the widest span between the pedicles.
measures.level_pattern: C3 19.2, C6 20.6 (cervical maximum), T1 17.7, T4 13.5 (column minimum), flat to T10 14.2, T11 15.3, T12 17.9, L1 to L3 about 19.5, L4 20.2, L5 23.4 (text 23.5). Separates T1/T2, T11/T12, L4/L5; not T3 to T10.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi -19.8% (C -19.4, T -20.7, L -18.1 computed). p. 144 (PDF 8), Fig. 10.
measures.error: SE 0.2 to 0.6 mm; median CV about 7% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: axial slab of the frame at pedicle height, filled foramen of the instance mask, maximum extent along X.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph inter-pedicular distance; magnification applies.

measures.name: Spinal canal depth (SCD), mm
measures.definition: Antero-posterior depth of the vertebral foramen in the top view; Fig. 1 draws it in the midline from the posterior body wall to the inner arch.
measures.level_pattern: 10.3 at C3 to C6 (column minimum), 11.0 C7, about 11.5 to 12.0 through the thoracic spine, 12.5 at L1 (maximum), falls to 11.2 at L3-L4, 11.4 at L5. Carries almost no level information.
measures.covariates: Largest difference in the paper: -31.8% against Panjabi (C -37.9, T -26.7, L -37.6 computed; -43.1 at C6). Implied Panjabi SCD 15 to 18 mm cervical; Inference: part landmark or method.
measures.error: SE 0.1 to 0.4 mm; median CV about 6% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: along Z at x = 0 from the dorsal body surface to the ventral lamina junction, same slab as SCW.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, posterior body wall to spinolaminar line; SCD/EPD cancels magnification.

measures.name: Spinal canal area (SCA), mm2
measures.definition: Area of the vertebral foramen in the top view, from the polygonised best-fit plane (triangle mesh).
measures.level_pattern: C3 149.7 to T1 169.4; T4 140.1 (column minimum); T12 177.8; L1 200.0 (maximum); L4 163.8 (lumbar minimum); L5 186.6. SCA/(SCW x SCD) 0.70 to 0.90.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi -31.7% (C -35.6, T -26.7, L -39.9; -43.5 at L4); minimum moved from Panjabi's T3 to T4 and from L3 to L4. Implied Panjabi lumbar maximum is at L5, not L1. p. 144 (PDF 8).
measures.error: SE 2.0 to 10.9 mm2; digitiser area error 1.71% (mean, two bars of about 2,250 mm2).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: area of the filled foramen in the frame's axial slab.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: not direct; about 0.78 x SCW (AP) x SCD (lateral), 0.70 at L5.

measures.name: Pedicle height and width (PDHl, PDHr, PDWl, PDWr), mm
measures.definition: Outer height and width of the pedicle section (Fig. 1 top views); section position along the pedicle not stated (Inference: isthmus, as Panjabi).
measures.levels: C3 to L5, left and right
measures.level_pattern: PDH falls C3 6.75 to C6 6.0, then T1 8.5, T3 9.8, flat to T7, rises to T11 14.25, T12 14.1, L1 13.1, flat to L4 13.2, L5 17.4. PDW C3 4.45 rises to T1 7.45, falls to 4.0 at T4-T5, rises to T12 7.55, drops to 5.55 at L1, rises to 11.55 at L5. Height always exceeds width; left and right within 0.8 mm. The T12/L1 PDW drop is not in the implied Panjabi values.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi PDH -16.1%, PDW -25.7% (largest -41% PDWl at T4 and L5); regional PDW C -15.0, T -27.7, L -31.7 computed. p. 144 (PDF 8).
measures.error: SE 0.1 to 0.8 mm; median CV 7 to 9% (PDH) and 12 to 13% (PDW), Inference.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: fit the pedicle axis from cross-section centroids, find the least-area perpendicular section, PDH its extent along frame Y, PDW across the axis in the axial plane; outer cortex.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: PDW from the pedicle oval on AP, PDH from lateral (thoracolumbar); magnification and angulation foreshorten.

measures.name: Pedicle cross-sectional area (PDAl, PDAr), mm2
measures.levels: C3 to L5, left and right
measures.level_pattern: About 28 at C3 to C5, almost constant cervical; T1 about 56.5 (local maximum), falls to about 32 at T4-T5, rises to about 95.5 at T12, drops to about 68 at L1, rises to about 157.6 at L5.
measures.error: SE 0.8 to 6.0 mm2; median CV about 14% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: area of the isthmus section.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: not direct; PDA/(PDH x PDW) 0.77 to 1.05.

measures.name: Pedicle length (PL), mm
measures.definition: Distance from the facet cortex to the anterior cortex of the body along the line of the pedicle sagittal inclination PDIs (McLain, Zindrick); the screw-path chord.
measures.projection: dry bone, 3D digitiser, axial (plane of PDIs)
measures.page: p. 145 (PDF 9); Fig. 1c p. 138 (PDF 2); Table 1; Table 4 p. 145
measures.level_pattern: T1 30.4, T2 27.5 (minimum), thoracic values 27.5 to 35.0 and noisy, T12 31.5, L1 41.4 (+9.9, largest step), L2 43.8 (maximum), L5 39.2. The T12/L1 step is also in Zindrick's series (Fig. 12).
measures.covariates: Shorter than Zindrick at every level by 15.6 to 28.3% (mean -22.1%); shorter than McLain at T1 to T6 by 2.9 to 26.2%. p. 145 (PDF 9), Table 4.
measures.error: SE 0.3 to 0.8 mm; median CV about 6% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: chord through the instance mask along the pedicle axis at angle PDIs from the dorsal facet cortex to the ventral body cortex.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: not direct; needs an axial image.

measures.name: Spinous process length (SPL), mm
measures.definition: Not defined in the text; Fig. 1c draws it from the spinous tip to the upper end-plate centroid (frame origin), Inference from the drawing.
measures.level_pattern: Steep cervical rise C3 25.6, C4 30.3, C5 33.6, C6 40.5, C7 46.9; almost constant thoracic 48.3 to 51.9; parabolic lumbar, L3 57.6 maximum, L5 50.6.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi -5.5% on average but larger at C5 to C7, T7, T10 to T12; lumbar about -23% (max -25.9% at L5). Implied Panjabi lumbar SPL 67 to 72; Inference: definitional difference.
measures.error: SE 0.4 to 1.5 mm; median CV about 5.5% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: distance from the cranial end-plate centroid to the farthest point of the spinous process subregion.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, upper end-plate midpoint to spinous tip; magnification applies.

measures.name: Transverse process width (TPW; written TPL three times in the text), mm
measures.definition: Tip-to-tip distance between the two transverse processes along X (Fig. 1 front views).
measures.level_pattern: C3 41.4 rising to C7 53.8, T1 63.8 (thoracic maximum), steep fall to T5 49.7, flat to T8, gradual fall to T12 41.0 (column minimum), L1 53.6, L3 71.4 (maximum), L5 71.3. C7/T1 +10.0 and T12/L1 +12.6 mm; both steps also in implied Panjabi values. TPW/EPWu 3.0 to 3.2 C3 to C6, 1.19 at T12, 1.48 at L1, 1.6 to 1.8 L2 to L5.
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi -15.6% (max -24.7% at L1); regional C -8.8, T -17.1, L -18.9 computed. p. 144 (PDF 8).
measures.error: SE 0.2 to 2.5 mm; median CV about 6% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: X extent between the most lateral voxels of the left and right transverse process subregions, ribs excluded.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph tip to tip; TPW/EPWu magnification-free.

measures.name: End-plate area, upper and lower (EPAu, EPAl), mm2
measures.definition: Area of the end-plate outline on the polygonised best-fit plane.
measures.projection: dry bone, 3D digitiser, plan view of end-plate plane
measures.level_pattern: EPAu 154.7 (C3) to 1151.8 (L4), 1127.3 at L5; EPAl 216.8 (C3) to 1199.3 (L4), 1054.1 at L5; lower larger than upper at every level; L3 EPAl misprinted 172.0. EPAu/(EPWu x EPDu) 0.77 to 0.94; EPAl/(EPWl x EPDl) 1.00 to 1.19 at C3 to C7 (inconsistent with a planar area bounded by those extents).
measures.covariates: EPAu -8.3% against Panjabi (max -20.7% at C7); EPAl -3.3% but +16.3% at C3 to C7. p. 144 (PDF 8).
measures.error: SE 3.8 to 35.5 mm2; median CV about 9.5% (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: end-plate surface voxels projected on their best-fit plane, filled-outline area.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: not direct; about 0.85 to 0.9 x AP width x lateral depth (not for the cervical lower end-plate values here).

measures.name: End-plate inclination, upper and lower (EPItu, EPItl), deg
measures.definition: Angle of each end-plate best-fit plane against the Z axis in the side view (Fig. 1b, Fig. 4 plane 1 and plane 2); sign convention not stated (positive matches the text's cephalad, Inference).
measures.level_pattern: Cervical both positive, lower smaller; thoracic upper positive (largest at top and bottom), lower negative; lumbar upper positive, lower changes sign at L2-L3, L5 lower 10.5. EPItl sign change at C7/T1 (+5.1 to -2.9). EPItl - EPItu matches the body wedge within 2 deg from T5 to L5 (Inference, computed).
measures.error: SE 0.1 to 5.2 deg (C3, C4 upper 4.1 and 5.2, Inference: outliers); digitiser angle error 0.68% (mean).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: planes fitted to cranial and caudal end-plate surfaces, angle to the frame X-Z plane about X.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, end-plate line against the perpendicular to the posterior wall.

measures.name: Pedicle sagittal inclination (PDIsl, PDIsr), deg
measures.definition: Axial-plane angle between the pedicle axis and the sagittal (midline) direction (Fig. 1 top views; Zindrick's definition). Left and right printed with opposite signs.
measures.page: p. 138 (PDF 2); p. 143 (PDF 7); Table 1; Table 3 and Fig. 11 p. 144 (PDF 8)
measures.levels: C3 to L5, left and right
measures.level_pattern: Mean magnitude about 41 at C3 to C6, 30 at C7, 24 at T1, falls to about 7 by T6-T7; sign reverses at T8 to T12 (magnitude 5 to 9, 8.6 at T8); L1 4.8 rising to 19.9 at L5. Fig. 11 and Table 3 use the right side (Inference).
measures.covariates: Against Panjabi (Table 3, right side): C3 -6.4 to C6 +20.6%, T4 to T7 -41 to -58.5%, T8 to T12 not meaningful, L1 -47.6 to L5 -29.3%. Against Zindrick T1 -8.3 to L5 -41.7%; Zindrick's implied T12 is slightly negative. p. 144 (PDF 8).
measures.error: SE 0.5 to 2.3 deg; left-right gap of level means up to 8.2 deg (C5).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: project the pedicle axis on the frame X-Z plane, angle to Z, average left and right magnitudes.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: not direct; needs an axial image.

measures.name: Pedicle transverse inclination (PDItl, PDItr), deg
measures.definition: Side-view angle between the pedicle axis and Z (Fig. 1 side views); sign convention not stated (positive matches the text's cephalad, Inference).
measures.levels: C3 to L5, left and right
measures.level_pattern: Caudal at C3-C4 (mean -5.65, -4.3), cephalad from C5 (transition C4-C5), cephalad through the thoracic spine (largest mean 7.8 at T3), caudal and increasing through the lumbar spine to about -7 at L5; sign change at T12/L1 (+3.75 to -1.65 mean).
measures.error: SE 0.2 to 1.4 deg; SD about 2.4 deg median (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: project the pedicle axis on the frame Y-Z plane, angle to Z.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, pedicle long axis against the perpendicular to the posterior wall (thoracolumbar).

level_details.detail: Not covered; C3 first level. C3 smallest for end-plate widths (13.8, 14.3), upper depth, posterior height and end-plate areas; shortest SPL (25.6); anterior height smallest at C5 (9.6); TPW 41.4 smallest cervical, T12 41.0 smaller.
Body widths, depths and heights fairly constant; canal depth 10.3 at C3 to C6; Inference: ordered by SPL (25.6, 30.3, 33.6) and TPW (41.4, 44.9, 47.6) and the PDIt sign change C4/C5.

EPWu +3.2 mm (15.8 to 19.0); SPL +6.4 to 46.9 (longest cervical); TPW +5.4; PDIs about 40 to 30 deg; SCW falls from its cervical maximum at C6 (20.6). Implied Panjabi TPW step much larger (about 49.5 to 66.6).

pearls_pitfalls.text: Indications: more accurate spine modelling, design of implants and instruments, and more precise diagnosis and management in Chinese Singaporeans.
Most implants were designed from Caucasian measurements; Chinese pedicles are about 26% narrower.

Pedicle width is too small for a 5 mm screw except at T1 and T10 to L5 per the text (Table 1 also gives more than 5 mm at C6, C7, T2); with the shorter upper-thoracic PL and the T8 to T12 divergence, the authors say a transpedicular screw may not be feasible.
T8 to T12 pedicles show a slight divergence (about 7 deg) instead of convergence, which may affect screw placement.
Canal depth and area about 32% smaller than Panjabi's may affect surgical management, especially of low back pain; the mid-thoracic minimum (T4) is the critical vascular zone (ref 2).
The posterior body wall was used for the frame because it is fairly consistent and least affected by osteophytes.
Pedicle length is comparable across studies only with the same definition (facet cortex to anterior cortex along PDIs); McLain's older, mostly female cadavers may explain a smaller gap.

Inference: 'sagittal inclination' (PDIs) is the axial-plane medial angle and 'transverse inclination' (PDIt) the sagittal-plane tilt; the names are easy to invert, and the paper's divergence/convergence words are inconsistent.
Inference: the cervical and L1 to L3 bodies are taller behind than in front (VBHa/VBHp 0.85 to 0.97); only L5 is taller in front (1.10), so lordosis lies in the discs and L5.
Inference: the anterior 5 mm fixation hole sits where the anterior cortex and anterior height are measured.
Inference: a 10.3 mm bony cervical canal depth in unselected cadavers sits at the usual stenosis threshold; Panjabi's implied value is 15 to 18 mm, so a landmark difference is likely.
Inference: cervical EPAl exceeds EPWl x EPDl (1.00 to 1.19); do not treat those areas as planar.

instructions.text: Build each vertebra's frame on the posterior body wall (normal = antero-posterior axis) with the origin at the upper end-plate centroid; measure in that frame, not scanner axes.
Measure bilateral pedicle quantities on both sides and use the mean of magnitudes; Inference: a left-right PDIs gap far above 8.2 deg suggests a wrong frame.

Place T1 by a joint step from C7: TPW +10 mm to the thoracic maximum, EPWu +5.7 mm, PDW +1.8 mm to a local maximum, PDA to a local maximum, EPItl positive to negative; weight TPW and the pedicle over EPWu (Panjabi's implied EPWu step is 2.7 mm); confirm with ribs (not in this paper).

Place T12/L1 by TPW minimum at T12 (41.0) and +12.6 mm at L1; Inference: TPW/EPWu about 1.2 at T12, 1.5 at L1, 1.6 to 1.8 below; confirm with PL +10 mm and PDIt sign change; treat the PDW drop and the L1 SCA maximum as weak cues.

Place L5 as the only level with VBHa > VBHp (1.10), EPItl about 10 deg, PDH about 17 mm, PDW about 11.5 mm, canal +3 mm and end-plate width dip against L4; Inference: in a transitional spine these may sit one level off, so decode with the sequence.
Do not use canal depth (10.3 to 12.5 mm everywhere) or canal width at T3 to T10 (13.5 to 14.2 mm) to tell levels apart.
Do not use end-plate width to order T1 to T6; use end-plate depth, which rises nearly linearly T1 to T12.
Order C3 to C5 by SPL and TPW (each about 3 to 5 mm per level) and the PDIt sign change at C4/C5, jointly, since the SD is close to the step.
Inference: do not use the sign of PDIs at T8 to T12 as a level marker until confirmed on CT.
Read pedicle length as the facet-to-anterior-cortex chord along the pedicle axis, never the short pedicle.
Inference: check mask end-plate planes by EPItl - EPItu roughly equal to atan((VBHa - VBHp)/EPD), within about 2 deg from T5 to L5 in this table.
Inference: estimate areas from two radiographs as about 0.85 to 0.9 x width x depth (end-plate) and 0.7 to 0.9 x SCW x SCD (canal); work in ratios because magnification is unknown.

For a Chinese patient against a Panjabi prior expect body widths about 10%, depths 15%, pedicle heights 16%, pedicle widths 26%, TPW 16%, canal width 20% and canal depth 32% smaller (canal depth with caution); cervical EPAl and some cervical SPL are larger.
Flag T3 to T9 pedicles under 5 mm wide (means 4.0 to 4.95 mm here).
Measure cervical upper end-plate width between the uncinate bases, the lower width across the whole body.
Inference: take SPL from the upper end-plate centroid to the spinous tip, as Fig. 1c draws it.
Take no anomaly prior from this paper: it reports none and gives no numbering method.

bordercall: (a) Anomaly priors: none. No transitional or numerical variant reported; 220 = 10 x 22 levels; screening unknown. p. 137 (PDF 1).

(b) Held measures given here per level C3 to L5 (mean +/- SE, n = 10 by Inference): EPWu, EPWl, EPDu, EPDl, VBHa, VBHp, SCW, SCD, PDH and PDW left and right. Addable: SCA, PDA, EPAu, EPAl, TPW, SPL, PL (T1 to L5), EPItu, EPItl, PDIs, PDIt. No facet dimensions or angles.

(b) Definition differences that bias a mask value: frame on the posterior wall with origin at the upper end-plate centroid (scanner axes would leak alignment); cervical EPWu between the uncinates (Fig. 1a); SPL from the end-plate centroid to the tip (Fig. 1c, Inference); PL is the screw-path chord; PDIs is the axial medial angle with opposite left-right signs; cervical EPAl exceeds width x depth; L3 EPAl misprinted 172.0; L4 PDHr printed 13.40.3.

(b) Strongest separators here: TPW at C7/T1 (+10.0) and T12/L1 (+12.6, about 3.6 pooled SDs), PL at T12/L1 (+9.9), L5 pedicle and VBHa/VBHp; these are shared with the comparison series. The T12/L1 PDW drop and the L1 SCA maximum are sample-specific (Inference, computed).

(c) Error: instrument about 1.3% of 20 mm, 0.68% of an angle, 1.7% of an area; between-specimen SD = 3.16 x SE (caveat: paper's own definition gives 10 x SE); median CVs EPW 3%, EPD 4 to 5%, VBH 4.5 to 6%, SCW 7%, SCD 6%, PDH 7 to 9%, PDW 12 to 13%, PL 6%, SPL 5.5%, TPW 6%, EPA and SCA 9.5%, PDA 14%; no observer reliability.

(d) Population factors, Chinese Singaporean against Panjabi (1 + regional mean difference / 100, C/T/L): EPW 0.86/0.91/0.90, EPD 0.90/0.83/0.85, VBHp 0.98/0.97/0.92, SCW 0.81/0.79/0.82, SCD 0.62/0.73/0.62, PDH 0.87/0.82/0.86, PDW 0.85/0.72/0.68, SPL 1.05/0.98/0.77, TPW 0.91/0.83/0.81, EPAu 0.92/0.92/0.90, EPAl 1.16/0.91/0.91, SCA 0.64/0.73/0.60; PL against Zindrick 0.78. Inference: canal and pedicle factors are far below body factors, so a single size factor cannot reproduce them; the factors also mix age (mean 65.7), unreported sex and method.
(d) Size: mean height 1.66 m (1.59 to 1.72), weight 61.6 kg (50 to 70), no per-specimen data or size regression; sex not reported; age 56 to 77 with no age analysis. p. 137 (PDF 1).
(d) Inference: Panjabi values implied by Tables 1 and 2 (value / (1 + difference / 100)) give a per-level cross-check for a Panjabi-built generator.
